2027-07-22.title: St Mary Magdalene · Thursday of the ninth week after Pentecost
readings: If anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: God has given us the ministry of reconciliation
Mary Magdalene at the tomb: “Mary!” “Rabbouni!” and “I have seen the Lord”
2027-07-22.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Ninth Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam keeps today the memory of St Mary Magdalene (വി. മഗ്ദലേന മറിയം). In the Roman calendar, since 2016, she is honoured with the title Apostle of the Apostles; the title is much older, and was given to her by teachers of the Church such as St Thomas Aquinas, because she was the first sent to announce the resurrection. The Panchangam gives the readings of the weekday only.
2027-07-22.verse: Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
theo: Who was Mary Magdalene? The Gospels tell us less than we would like, and what they tell us is enough. She came from Magdala, a town on the Sea of Galilee. Luke names her among the women who followed Jesus and “provided for them out of their resources”: “Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.” She was a woman whom the Lord had delivered, and she did not go away afterwards. She was standing “near the cross of Jesus” with his mother and the other women; she saw where he was buried; and on the first day of the week she is the first to come to the tomb. We should say plainly what the Gospels do not say: they never say that she is the sinful woman of Luke chapter 7 or Mary of Bethany. An older tradition of the Western Church joined these women together, but the Church today keeps them distinct, and we read her as the Gospel gives her to us: a woman healed by the Lord, a faithful friend at the cross, and the first witness of the resurrection. Today's Epistle is the best commentary on her life: “So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!”

Now follow her through the Gospel. “Early on the first day of the week, while it was still dark, Mary Magdalene came to the tomb and saw that the stone had been removed.” In her first fear she runs to Peter and the beloved disciple, and they run to the tomb, see the linen wrappings, and return to their homes. But “Mary stood weeping outside the tomb.” The disciples have gone home, and she stays. She bends and looks in, and sees two angels in white who ask: “Woman, why are you weeping?” She answers: “They have taken away my Lord, and I do not know where they have laid him.” Then she turns and sees Jesus standing there, “but she did not know that it was Jesus.” He asks: “Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?” Supposing him to be the gardener, she says: “Sir, if you have carried him away, tell me where you have laid him, and I will take him away.” She speaks as a woman who has only one wish: to give the body of the Lord an honourable place.

Then comes the shortest and greatest sentence of the Gospel: “Jesus said to her, ‘Mary!’ She turned and said to him in Hebrew, ‘Rabbouni!’ (which means Teacher).” The risen Lord is not first known by sight or by argument. He is known when he calls her by name, as the Good Shepherd calls his own sheep by name. And then he gives her a mission: “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’” She must not cling to the Lord as he was; a new relationship is beginning, in which he will be with his Church by the Spirit. And look at the words: “my brothers.” They were the men who fled, and he calls them brothers. “Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord’; and she told them that he had said these things to her.” This is why the Church has called her the apostle of the apostles, the one who was sent to the Apostles.

Paul's words in the Epistle describe what she became: “All this is from God, who reconciled us to himself through Christ, and has given us the ministry of reconciliation; that is, in Christ God was reconciling the world to himself, not counting their trespasses against them, and entrusting the message of reconciliation to us. So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us.” Mary Magdalene is the first ambassador of the risen Christ. She is sent to men who had abandoned the Lord, with a message of forgiveness: my brothers, my Father and your Father. In our tradition the morning prayer, Sapro, is the prayer of daybreak that remembers the resurrection, and in the dark of the monsoon mornings many Christians rise early to pray, as she came to the tomb while it was still dark. Let us ask her intercession: for the grace to stay when others go home, to seek the Lord with love even through tears, to listen for him to call us by name, and to go and tell others, with joy, “I have seen the Lord.”
outline: Ask: when I cannot find the Lord, do I go home, or do I stay and keep looking?
Magdala, the seven demons, the cross and the burial; a faithful friend. She is not the sinful woman of Luke 7; the Gospel gives her as it is.
While it was still dark; the angels' question; seeking with tears and love.
The Lord is known by being called by name; do not hold on, but go.
The ministry of reconciliation; sent to the brothers who had fled.
live: When prayer feels dry, stay ten minutes longer in front of the cross or the tabernacle, telling the Lord everything, even your tears.
Take five minutes in silence and ask the Lord to call you by name; remember that in baptism he has already done so.
Tell one person this week, simply, what the risen Lord has done for you; and reconcile with someone who has been distant from you.
2027-07-22.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen from the dead, you called Mary Magdalene by name in the garden and sent her to your brothers with the first word of the resurrection. We thank you for her faithfulness at the cross, her tears at the tomb and her joy in announcing that she had seen the Lord. Make us new creations in you. When we cannot find you, give us the love that stays and seeks. Call us by name, and when we hear your voice, send us as ambassadors of your reconciliation. Through the prayers of St Mary Magdalene, apostle of the apostles, strengthen the faith of your Church and lead us to see you, face to face, in the light of your kingdom. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbono the Lord who stood in the garden and called her by name comes to us under the form of bread and wine, and sends us out in peace with the same word: Go and tell.
conn: John 19:25: “standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene”; Mark 15:47: she saw where he was laid.
John 10:3: the Good Shepherd “calls his own sheep by name and leads them out”; Isaiah 43:1: “I have called you by name, you are mine.”
Luke 8:2: “Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out”; Revelation 21:5: “See, I am making all things new.”
fathers: She who stayed at the tomb to seek him found him, because she remained, and the love that seeks is the love that finds; the disciples had gone home and she kept on weeping and looking (Homilies on the Gospels 25, in substance).

Because a woman had announced to the man the first word of death, so a woman is first to announce to the Apostles the word of life; thus she was made, as it were, the apostle of the apostles (Commentary on John, in substance).
magis: Mary Magdalene and the holy women, who came to finish anointing the body, were the first to encounter the Risen One; thus the women were the first messengers of Christ's resurrection to the Apostles themselves (in substance).
Christ entrusted to his Apostles the ministry of reconciliation, and in the Church the sacrament of penance carries it forward (in substance).

The decree of the Congregation for Divine Worship, 3 June 2016, raised the memorial of St Mary Magdalene in the Roman calendar to the rank of a feast, as the first witness of the Lord's resurrection and the apostle of the apostles (in substance).

quick: Mary Magdalene came to the tomb while it was still dark, and stayed weeping outside it after the disciples went home.
The risen Jesus called her by name, Mary, and she answered, Rabbouni; he sent her to his brothers.
Paul says that anyone in Christ is a new creation, and that God has entrusted us with the ministry of reconciliation.
2027-07-22.action: Stay a little longer in prayer today, and tell one person simply what the Lord has done for you.
2027-07-22.question: When I cannot find the Lord, do I go home, or do I stay and keep looking?

family.explain: Mary Magdalene loved Jesus very much. Early in the morning, while it was still dark, she went to the tomb and found it empty. The other friends of Jesus went home, but Mary stayed and cried. Then Jesus called her by name: Mary! At once she knew him. Jesus told her: Go and tell my brothers. And she ran to say, I have seen the Lord! Jesus calls each one of us by name, too, and he sends us to tell others about his love.
family.intention: We pray for those who are sad or who miss someone they love, and for the courage to tell others about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How does Jesus call my name? What is one joyful thing I can tell someone about him?”

illus: After the death of her teenage son, a woman in a parish near Kollam began to go to the church garden before dawn every day. She sat on the stone bench under the jackfruit tree and wept quietly, as the first rain of the day fell on the leaves. Weeks went by, and she spoke to no one. One morning the old sacristan, coming to ring the bell for the early prayer, passed her and said her name softly, as he had said it for thirty years: Leelamma. She looked up for the first time in many weeks, and said later that it was as if someone had opened a window. She had not known, she said, that she was still known. She began to speak again, first to the sacristan, then to the priest, and, in time, to other mothers who had lost children. People say she became a ministry of consolation in the parish, and she always said that it began with a single name spoken in the dark.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, risen from the dead, you called Mary Magdalene by name. Call us too, and send us to tell others that we have seen the Lord. Amen.
share: Mary stood weeping outside the tomb (John 20:11). When have I stayed with the Lord in sadness?
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” (John 20:16). How have I heard the Lord call my name?
Go to my brothers and say to them (John 20:17). To whom does the Lord send me this week?
interc: For the Church, that, like Mary Magdalene, she may announce the resurrection with joy.
For women and men who suffer, that they may be consoled by the Risen Lord.
For those who weep for the dead, that they may hear the Lord call them by name.
For reconciliation in families and communities, that we may be ambassadors for Christ.
For those who have fallen away, that the Lord may call them back as his brothers and sisters.

term: An Aramaic word meaning my teacher, my master, a more affectionate form of Rabbi. Mary Magdalene uses it when she recognises the risen Lord, and John tells us that it means Teacher. It shows the warmth of a disciple who has found her Lord again.
kidsaint: The first to say, I have seen the Lord

Mary Magdalene was a friend of Jesus. When Jesus died, she was so sad. Very early on Sunday morning she went to the tomb and cried. Then someone called her name: Mary! It was Jesus! He was alive. He told her: Go and tell my friends. And she ran and said: I have seen the Lord! Lesson: Jesus knows our names, and when we meet him, we want to tell everyone the good news.

homily: Dear friends, today we remember St Mary Magdalene. The Gospels tell us that she was a woman from Magdala whom Jesus had delivered, that she stood near his cross, and that she came to the tomb early on the first day of the week while it was still dark (John 20:1). She is not the sinful woman of Luke chapter 7; the Gospel does not say so, and we read her as the Gospel gives her. She was a faithful friend.

Peter and the other disciple saw the empty tomb and went home. But Mary stood weeping outside the tomb (John 20:11). She stayed and kept looking. Two angels asked her why she was weeping, and then Jesus himself asked her, and she thought he was the gardener. Then Jesus said her name: Mary! She turned and said, Rabbouni! (John 20:16). The Lord knows his own sheep by name.

Jesus said: Do not hold on to me, but go to my brothers and say to them, I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God. And Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, I have seen the Lord (John 20:17–18). She was the first to announce the resurrection, and so the Church calls her the apostle of the apostles. St Paul says: God has given us the ministry of reconciliation, and we are ambassadors for Christ (2 Corinthians 5:18, 20).
Let us ask St Mary Magdalene to teach us to stay and seek the Lord with love, to listen as he calls us by name, and to go and tell others, with joy, that we have seen the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine you are very sad because you cannot find someone you love. Mary Magdalene was like that on the first Easter morning. She went to the tomb while it was still dark, and she cried. Then someone said, Mary! And she knew at once it was Jesus, because he said her name in his special way. He was alive! Jesus knows your name, too. And like Mary, we can run to tell our friends: Jesus is alive, I have seen the Lord!

intro: On Thursday of the ninth week after Pentecost, St Mary Magdalene: a woman delivered, the one who stayed and wept, called by name, and sent to the brothers.

She is not the sinful woman of Luke 7.

And the one who was seated on the throne said, “See, I am making all things new.”
points.apply: Thank the Lord for one way in which he has made you new, and speak of it.

sub: The disciples went home; she stayed.
The love that seeks is the love that finds.
q: Scarcely had I passed them, when I found him whom my soul loves.
But Mary stood weeping outside the tomb.
points.apply: When prayer is dry, stay ten minutes longer and tell the Lord everything.

sub: Known by being called by name.

sub: Sent to the brothers who had fled.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’
points.apply: Tell one person what the risen Lord has done for you, and reconcile with someone who is distant.

concl: The Lord is found by love that stays, and known when he calls us by name.
The first to see the risen Lord was the first sent to announce him, and so are we.
2027-07-22.resolve: Stay and seek, listen for your name, and go and tell: I have seen the Lord.
